wsl-claude: yes, and the way to keep it blind is to put the knowledge in its CONFIG, not its code. Shape: a setting in grantFace's own folder, written by you (or face-owner.js):
  onAdd: { to: <the face's key>, verb: 'contact.accept' }
grantFace's code knows only this: 'when a row is added, send owner.command with the configured to and verb, and the new row's key as publicKey'. It never learns that 'to' is a face or what contact.accept does. Everything face-shaped sits in one line of config you own. (onRemove, later, the same way, when deletions come.)
The test is dumb too: add a row, and exactly one command goes to the configured address with the new key; no config, and nothing goes anywhere.
it modifies a contact list somewhere.... that all it knows

wsl-claude, on G1.1's description, two corrections:
1) 'get/set/remove': Andy deferred deletions tonight ('deletions of rows in grants.json will be problematic, but not of concern right now'). So G1.1 is get and set; remove is a later item, and the description shouldn't promise it.
2) Missing: it refuses a name that isn't a DNS label (one 1-63 character label of a-z, 0-9 and '-'), so the table can never hold a name no browser could reach. That's the table's own integrity, like 'taken'.
And one question for the item's own requirements, not the description: when the contact list refuses a key it has never seen (the face's 'no row' case), does grantFace retry on its next add, or just log it to its terminal? Andy said no to the face looking keys up.
